sources.entry: PySide6 - Qt for Python offers the official Python bindings for Qt, largely API-compatible with PyQt6 but with different licensing.

summary.one_liner: Qt For Python (pyside-setup), the build tooling for the official PySide6 Qt bindings for Python, which uses the Shiboken binding generator.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes the Python Qt bindings project, which provides access to the Qt framework from Python and includes generator tools for producing bindings for C++ libraries. It builds three components through one setup.py script: the shiboken6 Python module, the shiboken6-generator executable, and the PySide6 bindings. A --build-type option selects which components to build or package. The README lists many build flags covering Qt module subsets, rpath, standalone Qt embedding, macOS SDK and deployment target, OpenSSL on Windows, and development options such as reusing builds and skipping CMake. It also describes a CMake super project and Qt Creator setup for development. The README does not describe end-user API usage.
use_cases: generate Python bindings for C++ libraries
package PySide6 standalone with embedded Qt libraries
develop or debug the Shiboken binding generator
set up a Qt Creator CMake project for PySide6
how_to_run: Requires Python 3.10+, CMake, and Qt 6.x with qtpaths6 on PATH or passed via --qtpaths
notable: Official Python bindings for Qt, covering the complete Qt framework
Ships Shiboken, a generator usable for binding other C++ libraries
setup.py --build-type selects shiboken6, shiboken6-generator, pyside6 or all
Standalone option embeds Qt libraries into the PySide6 package on Linux and macOS
CMake super project and Qt Creator integration for development
caveats: Requires a Qt 6.x installation and CMake; build setup is involved
Windows OpenSSL support needs manual DLL directory configuration
Standalone packaging is not available on Windows through the same option, and some Qt packages linking OpenSSL directly are incompatible with standalone builds
